content.title: [Bug]: Non-canonical project fields (deadlines, custom scores, flags) silently dropped in scrum_find_items — custom_fields sparsely populated
content.body:
## Problem

`scrum_find_items` responses include a `custom_fields` field in `BacklogItemListing` but it is sparsely populated. Non-canonical project fields — deadlines, custom numeric scores, non-standard flags, and any board field outside the Scrum vocabulary — are silently dropped in the mapping layer.

The query and mapper are coupled to a fixed set of canonical field types (iteration, single-select, number, and a small named set). Any ProjectV2 field a team configures outside that set is invisible in `scrum_find_items` output, even when it contains decision-relevant data. There is no error or warning — the fields are simply absent.

## Impact

Agents cannot filter, sort, or act on project-specific metadata that teams commonly use: due dates, custom priority scores, effort estimates in non-standard fields. The data exists in GitHub Projects but never reaches the agent.

## Context — relationship to #216

Both issues affect `custom_fields` but in opposite directions:

| Issue | Problem |
|---|---|
| #216 | Canonical fields *incorrectly included* in `custom_fields` (duplication, noise) |
| This issue | Non-canonical fields *incorrectly excluded* from `custom_fields` (missing signal) |

The correct end state: `custom_fields` contains *only* non-canonical fields, and *all* of them. These two issues should be resolved together or in immediate sequence.

## Affected file

`src/adapters/github/internal/result-normalizer.ts` — field value mapping in `enrichListingCustomFields()`

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] All non-canonical field value types from the GraphQL response appear in `custom_fields`
- [ ] No non-canonical field type is silently dropped in the mapping layer
- [ ] Canonical fields (Title, Status, Type, Priority, Story Points, Sprint, Assignees, Labels, Milestone, Repository) are not present in `custom_fields` (handled by #216)
- [ ] Existing tests pass; new tests cover passthrough of non-canonical field types
- [ ] No changes to domain types, port interfaces, or use-case functions
